ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the vertical axis is surface water temperature, with the unit ℃, roughly from 10℃ to 30℃; the horizontal axis represents longitude changes from west to east along a certain latitude line in the Pacific Ocean. There are two curves in the figure: the August curve is basically above the February curve, and across almost the entire Pacific section, the water temperature in August is higher than in February; the water temperature range is roughly from the teens Celsius to the twenties Celsius, warmer in the west and gradually colder in the east. Then reason: Along the same latitude line, seawater in August is generally warmer than in February, indicating that August is the local summer, and this latitude line is located in the Northern Hemisphere. The water temperature values are not the year-round high temperatures near the equator, but have relatively obvious seasonal differences, and they show the characteristic of the North Pacific subtropical sea area being warm in the west and cold in the east, which accords with the surface water temperature distribution near about the 30°N latitude line. Therefore, this latitude line may be 30°N.

<image1>

method.method_draft: First describe the image: note that the August line is above the February line across nearly the whole Pacific transect and that the values are roughly in the teens to upper 20s °C, with a warm western side and cooler eastern side. From the text, understand that the task is to infer the latitude of this Pacific zonal transect. Apply the geographic bridge: August is summer in the Northern Hemisphere, so the latitude must be north, and the moderate subtropical SSTs plus strong seasonal contrast and east-west current pattern correspond best to about 30°N. Conclude the latitude is 30°N.
method.CoT_raw: 先描述图像：图中纵轴为表层水温，单位为℃，大致从10℃到30℃；横轴表示沿太平洋某纬线自西向东的经度变化。图中有两条曲线，8月曲线基本位于2月曲线之上，几乎整个太平洋断面8月水温都高于2月；水温范围大致在十几摄氏度到二十多摄氏度，西部较暖，东部逐渐偏冷。再推理：同一纬线上海水8月普遍比2月暖，说明8月为当地夏季，该纬线位于北半球。水温数值不是赤道附近的全年高温，而有较明显季节差异，且呈现北太平洋副热带海区西暖东冷的特征，符合约30°N纬线附近的表层水温分布。因此该纬线可能为30°N。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Uses the graph’s seasonal contrast and temperature magnitude as the main route: identify hemisphere from which month is warmer, then narrow latitude from the absolute sea-surface temperatures and Pacific current pattern. This is the straightforward physically grounded inference for this single-answer problem.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the graph as sea-surface temperature along a Pacific latitude line: the vertical axis is temperature in °C, the horizontal axis spans Pacific longitudes from about 120°E across 180° to about 120°W. The dashed August curve stays much warmer than the February curve, mostly about 20–28°C versus about 12–23°C, and temperatures are warmer in the western/central Pacific than near the eastern Pacific margin.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt to know the figure is “surface water temperature variation along a certain latitude in the Pacific” and that the requested output is the possible latitude.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the rule that August warmer than February indicates the Northern Hemisphere. The observed SST range is too cool and seasonally variable for the equator/tropics near 0°–10°, but too warm for high latitudes; it matches the North Pacific subtropical-midlatitude belt. The west-warm/east-cool pattern also fits Kuroshio influence in the western North Pacific and California cold current/upwelling in the eastern North Pacific around 30°N.
